feature: Pick a transition at the cut, from tiles of your own two clips
summary: How one clip becomes the next is chosen in one place, at the cut: the tiles there show your two clips themselves and name both of them. A recording's right-click has one Transition… row instead of Fade In, Fade Out, Fade In and Out and Add Transition, and fading from black lives on the free end's handle.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Two recordings butted together on V1 (drop a second one onto the end of the first).

try.do: Right-click the first recording: one Transition… row, no fade rows (before: Add Transition ▸, plus Fade In and Out, Fade In, Fade Out under More).
try.shotNote: BEFORE. Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

AFTER. Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Choose Transition…, or click right on the cut: the tiles open there, named Tutorial Sample → b-roll, each one your two clips.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Rest the pointer on Cube: its tile plays the turn. Its tip reads Cube: Tutorial Sample turns into b-roll.
Click Cube: it goes on the cut as a band over both clips.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Right-click the band: Transition… opens the same tiles, beside Length, Curve and Remove Transition.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick the first recording and drag the diamond at its top left corner to the right: it fades up from black. The corner that meets b-roll has no diamond.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Does Transition… in the clip's right-click feel like the one obvious way, now the fade rows are gone?
Can you tell the tiles apart at a glance now they show your own clips at 26 points tall, or do the turning kinds read too small?
Where a clip meets others at both ends, is Transition ▸ At the Start… / At the End… clear enough?
Is the line naming both clips (Tutorial Sample → b-roll) the right amount of words above the tiles?
rough: The line naming both clips above the tiles is not in the mock (video-transition-wt.html #transPick); it is the user's own ask of 2026-10-29 that the picker say what happens between the two clips, approved as written that day.
The tiles show the two clips' real frames instead of the mock's colour swatches, and rest part way through, playing only under the pointer: the user's own ask of 2026-10-29.

No walk can rest the pointer on a tile or press one inside the picker on this Mac, nor click the timeline by pointer (walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-26), so hover playback and the click on the cut were checked by build and by eye in code, not watched. a-click-on-the-cut-opens-its-tiles-walk is the pointer proof and waits on that task.
A clip's right-click no longer puts a transition on both its ends at once; ⌘T with several clips picked still does every cut among them.
Titles and pictures keep Fade In and Out: they meet no clip, and their fade is how they come and go (the user asked for that row on 2026-10-19).
The real frames are read at 192 pixels, so on two recordings of the same dark screen most tiles are mostly dark.
